summary.name: Pixel Art (category: Digital and 3D Aesthetics; provenance: explicit). Pixel art and a 16-bit sprite appearance are explicitly requested.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: pixel art and a 16-bit sprite appearance, built on a low logical resolution, a limited palette, whole-pixel placement and deliberate pixel clusters. The 320x180 canvas and 32-color palette are optional examples, not requirements. Source-video details were not verified.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: sprites and scenes on a fixed logical grid. Inferred fits: game trailers, looping social clips, and explainers using 2:1 pixel isometric tiles. Compatibility lists also name Pixel Art for typography and burst motions and for lighting-state progression, when the scene supports them.
summary.limitations: Keep smoothing off and scaling integer. Avoid anti-aliased edges, arbitrary-angle rotation, Three.js perspective and post-effects that blend palette indices. Palette cycling must stay discrete. Two-color contrast checks do not cover text over animated or textured frames. Matter.js is 2D rigid-body only, not fluid or soft-body. 32 colors is not a universal 16-bit rule.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent: the #18253A swatch is illustrative, not a required canvas color; choose the background from subject, lighting and mood. Six suggested base colors: #18253A, #F3EBD3, #426A76, #8AA386, #D3A45E, #B56D6F. These are not approved exact colors; task-provided colors override them, and gradients are disabled. Checked pairs: foreground on background 12.923:1; accent_1 with foreground 4.961:1; accent_2 and accent_3 as backgrounds with the background token as text 5.616:1 and 6.773:1. accent_4 with background (3.944:1) is decorative only. Recheck composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: key poses with few in-between frames; delivery frame rate may exceed exposure rate. Palette cycling suits water, neon or day-night change without moving silhouettes. Keep whole-pixel placement and nearest-neighbour scaling. Optional references, only when scene assets support them: gaze (motion-006, needs eye layers or a rig), chapter handoff (motion-012), storytelling (motion-015), glyph, zoom, burst and phrase cuts (motion-037 to motion-040), and lighting states (motion-042). Interaction is unspecified; pointer behaviour applies only to interactive delivery.
summary.audio: Unspecified in the input; no audio asset is supplied or required. Inferred options, none mandatory: a chiptune-style track whose beat table schedules poses and palette steps (style-105), or silence for a schematic preview. Source reviews verified no audio synchronization, so beat timing must come from actually inspected audio. Voiceover and captions are unspecified.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads are specified, and none are mandatory. Needs depend on the chosen references: local fonts, glyph or approved mark geometry for typography and punctuation motions, eye layers or a rig for gaze, and named environment layers per lighting state. Do not invent copy or brand marks. Motion-040 evidence came from a user-supplied recording, which is not part of this metadata.
summary.combinations: style-105 (beat-table timing): schedules key-pose swaps and palette rotations; keep cycling discrete, with no full-screen flashing and no live-analysis drift. style-077 (2:1 pixel isometric tile grid): tile-based layout with labels in a separate crisp text layer, using the six primary colors and no arbitrary-angle rotation. Use hybrids only when music or a strict tile grid is needed; avoid Three.js perspective.
summary.productionApproach: Renderer: Canvas 2D draws indexed sprites at integer coordinates on a fixed offscreen canvas and owns the visuals; PixiJS or p5.js are optional layers with explicit, time-driven redraws. Motion: a GSAP paused timeline, with one owner per animated property; Matter.js is optional, using precomputed seeded states. Pipeline: HyperFrames assembles, times, syncs and exports; Remotion only on a recorded fallback. chroma-js validates colors; Aseprite is optional for palettes and sheets. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks, plus decoded frames.
